deep.reconstruction:
The page holds two unrelated pieces of work, written on reused official paper. The printed or copied Italian heading reads 'Cancelleria delegatizia di Graubünden … consiglio minore'.

(A) Top: an algebraic computation with a λ-th root of unity.
- Given are real numbers 0 ≤ x_ν < 1 for ν = 0,…,λ−1, with S = Σx_ν. A further condition 'Σx_ν ≥ n' (or '= n'; the reading is uncertain) appears beside them.
- Riemann defines ξ(α) = x_0 + x_1 α + … + x_{λ−1} α^{λ−1} − S.
- Since ξ(1) = 0, ξ is divisible by 1−α. His first, struck-out, attempt writes ξ(α)/(1−α) = y_0 + y_1 α + … + y_{λ−1} α^{λ−1}, normalised by Σy_ν = 0. Modulo α^λ = 1 the quotient is only fixed up to multiples of 1+α+…+α^{λ−1}, hence this normalisation. He then expands (1−α)Σy_k α^k = (y_0−y_{λ−1}) + (y_1−y_0)α + … and starts to bound the differences, e.g. y_{λ−1}−y_{λ−2} < 1 and y_1−y_0 < 1. He writes y_1 = y_0 + Δ_1.
- The surviving line computes instead ξ(α)(1−α) = (x_0 − S − x_{λ−1}) + (x_1 − x_0 + S)α + (x_2−x_1)α² + … + (x_{λ−1}−x_{λ−2})α^{λ−1}. This is valid modulo α^λ − 1 (my addition: the term −x_{λ−1}α^λ has been reduced to −x_{λ−1}). So α is a λ-th root of unity.
- The aim appears to be relating fractional-part vectors to elements of Z[α] divisible by (1−α), as in Kummer's cyclotomic theory. The purpose cannot be fixed from this page.

(B) Main body: draft of a letter on Abelian integrals.
- Riemann recalls a remark from his lectures. Let T be a Riemann surface of genus p, cut along p pairs of cross-cuts a_i, b_i into a simply connected T'.
- An everywhere-finite integral (first kind) w maps T' onto a surface in the w-plane. This image consists of p 'sheet pairs', each bounded by two pairs of congruent curves (the period translates). The sheet pairs are joined by 2(p−1) simple branch points.
- Modern gloss (mine): these are the 2p−2 zeros of the holomorphic differential dw, i.e. a canonical divisor. At each zero dw ~ (z−z0)dz, so w−w0 ~ (z−z0)², a simple winding point.
- He says this picture underlies all his computations, including those for the integrals he calls u, and holds in higher cases too.
- For the correspondent's special case p=2, one can obtain a one-sheeted surface S. To see what the p-sheeted picture becomes, attach a congruent copy of S along one side of the lines; the figure is coloured blue, red and black.
- Going around two branch points together (one in S, one in the copy), one returns to the start only after three circuits. If the two points coincide, the surface winds three times about that point. Gloss: a double zero of dw gives w−w0 ~ (z−z0)³, a cone angle of 6π.
- The correspondent's integral is then a special case of w = ∫ φ(s,z) dz / (∂F/∂s), on the curve F(s,z)=0. Here φ is the square of a 'so-called Abelian function', meaning the 2(p−1) zeros of φ/F_s coincide in pairs.
- Modern: the differential has divisor 2D with deg D = p−1, so D is a theta characteristic, and φ is the square of a section of a square root of the canonical bundle (Riemann's root functions).
- The next page continues: the p−1 double zeros can be taken as common starting points of p−1 pairs of cuts. The w-image becomes a parallelogram with p−1 parallelograms cut out, whose vertices are the double zeros. For p=2 this is a parallelogram with one parallelogram removed. This case is needed for certain differential equations.
errors: Formula line: the identity ξ(α)(1−α) = … holds only modulo α^λ = 1. This is implicit (α a primitive λ-th root of unity) and not stated.
The struck-out (1−α)·Σy_kα^k expansion appears to end with (y_{λ−2} − y_{λ−1})α^{λ−1}; it should be (y_{λ−1} − y_{λ−2})α^{λ−1}. This could be a slip or a misreading, and it was abandoned anyway.

In 'p Blattpaaren … durch 2(p−1) einfache Verzweigungspunkte' the count is consistent with the degree of the canonical divisor, 2p−2. The claim that cuts can always be chosen so the image is p such sheet pairs is stated without proof (as expected in a letter).
No mathematical errors otherwise detected. The threefold winding at a coincident pair of simple branch points is correct.

results.what: Reduction of ξ(α)(1−α) for ξ = Σx_kα^k − Σx_k with α^λ = 1 and 0 ≤ x_k < 1 (cyclotomic / fractional-part computation)
results.modern_name: Elementary computation in Z[ζ_λ], divisibility by (1−ζ)

results.what: Image of the canonically cut surface T' under a first-kind integral w: p sheet pairs bounded by congruent (period-translated) curves, joined at 2p−2 simple branch points (zeros of dw)
results.modern_name: Flat/translation-surface structure of a holomorphic abelian differential; zeros of dw form a canonical divisor of degree 2g−2
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (Theorie der Abel'schen Functionen 1857, and lectures); polygon representation later in Klein and others

results.what: Coalescing two simple branch points gives a point of threefold winding (double zero of dw)
results.modern_name: Cone point of angle 6π; stratum H(2,…) of abelian differentials

results.what: Integral ∫φ dz/F_s with φ the square of an 'Abelian function', i.e. all 2p−2 zeros double; image is a parallelogram with p−1 parallelograms removed (next page)
results.modern_name: Abelian differential with divisor 2D, D a theta characteristic (square of a root function); flat picture of a translation surface in the stratum H(2,…,2)
results.usually_credited_to: Root functions: Riemann/Weber, Prym (1860s–70s); polygon/flat picture of such strata: modern translation-surface theory (Masur, Veech, Kontsevich–Zorich for spin components)

deep.surprise_reason: The general picture of the w-image of the cut surface is Riemann's own and known from his lectures. Somewhat notable is the explicit flat-geometric description for differentials with only double zeros (squares of root functions, i.e. theta characteristics): a parallelogram with p−1 parallelograms removed. This anticipates the translation-surface viewpoint. Still, it is a letter-level remark without new theorems, likely to a student or correspondent such as Prym (identity unsure).

The number of simple branch points 2(p−1) equals the degree 2g−2 of a canonical divisor.
A double zero of dw gives w ~ t^3 locally, i.e. threefold winding (one returns after three circuits).
